findings.control_name: No credentials in recognised provider formats
findings.message: No credentials in recognised provider formats: matched in 1 location(s).

evidence.note: matched \bAKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}\b

findings.remediation_hint: Treat every matched key as compromised: rotate it at the provider first, then remove it from the code. Removing it from the working tree is not enough on its own -- it stays in git history, so purge or rotate. Afterwards read the value from the environment or a secret manager.

findings.remediation_hint: Build the URL at runtime from environment variables, or store the whole URL in one environment variable. Rotate the password that appeared in source; it must be assumed known.

findings.remediation_hint: Cap the request size at the framework level, allowlist the extensions and content types you accept, and write the file under a name you generate rather than the one the client supplied.

findings.message: Rate limiting middleware registered: no match anywhere in scope.

evidence.note: searched file contents of 2 indexed file(s) against 8 pattern(s); found nothing

findings.remediation_hint: Install and register a limiter for the framework in use -- flask-limiter, slowapi for FastAPI, express-rate-limit for Express, or DRF's throttle classes -- and back it with a shared store (Redis) if you run more than one process, otherwise each worker counts separately.

no guard within 4 lines above or 4 below, not crossing a blank line
searched 1 indexed file(s) for credential endpoint; 2 matched, 0 satisfied

findings.remediation_hint: Put a tight, explicit limit on each credential endpoint -- on the order of a handful of attempts per minute per IP and per account -- separate from whatever global default the app uses. Count failures, not requests, and prefer a shared store so the limit survives a restart.

findings.message: 1 high-entropy string literal(s) sit in source where a secret store should be used.

evidence.note: Shannon entropy 4.12 bits/char over 20 characters

findings.remediation_hint: Move the value into the environment or a secret manager and read it at startup. If the literal is genuinely not a secret -- a fixture, a public key, a test vector -- move it under a tests or fixtures path, which the entropy check already allowlists.

findings.remediation_hint: Read secret configuration from the environment with a required lookup that fails loudly at startup when it is missing, rather than from a literal with a default baked in.

findings.message: Debug mode not enabled: matched in 1 location(s).

evidence.note: matched \bdebug\s*=\s*True\b

findings.remediation_hint: Drive debug from an environment variable that defaults to off, so production cannot inherit a developer's setting. Never ship a configuration file in which debug is literally True.

findings.message: Response security headers set: no match anywhere in scope.

evidence.note: searched file contents of 2 indexed file(s) against 9 pattern(s); found nothing

findings.remediation_hint: Add the headers once in middleware rather than per response: helmet for Express, Talisman for Flask, or Django's SecurityMiddleware with the SECURE_* settings turned on. Start the CSP in report-only mode so you can tighten it without breaking the page.

findings.message: 2 of 4 HTTP route handler(s) are authenticated; 2 are not.

evidence.note: no guard within 4 lines above or 8 below, not crossing a blank line
no guard within 4 lines above or 8 below, not crossing a blank line

findings.remediation_hint: Attach an authentication dependency or decorator to each route that exposes user data or performs a state change. In Flask this is a login_required-style decorator above the route; in FastAPI it is a Depends(...) parameter on the handler, or a router-level dependencies list so new routes inherit it by default.

findings.message: All 2 password handling site(s) are backed by a hashing function.

evidence.note: guard found anywhere in the project: from werkzeug.security import check_password_hash, generate_password_hash
guard found anywhere in the project: from werkzeug.security import check_password_hash, generate_password_hash

findings.remediation_hint: Store a hash, never the password. Use bcrypt, argon2 or scrypt through a maintained library, and compare with the library's verify function rather than with the equality operator.

findings.control_name: No shell execution on request-derived input
findings.message: No shell execution on request-derived input: no match anywhere in scope.

evidence.note: searched file contents of 1 indexed file(s) against 7 pattern(s); found nothing

findings.remediation_hint: Call the program directly with an argument list and shell=False, so the shell never parses user data. Replace eval and pickle with a parser that only accepts the data you expect: json.loads, or yaml.safe_load.

findings.control_name: CORS policy is not wildcard or origin-reflecting
findings.message: CORS policy is not wildcard or origin-reflecting: no match anywhere in scope.

evidence.note: searched file contents of 2 indexed file(s) against 8 pattern(s); found nothing

findings.remediation_hint: Name the origins explicitly, from configuration rather than from the request. If credentials are allowed, a wildcard is not merely weak -- browsers reject the combination, so the code is broken as well as open.

findings.control_name: Password hashing algorithm is not MD5 or SHA-1
findings.message: Password hashing algorithm is not MD5 or SHA-1: no match anywhere in scope.

evidence.note: searched file contents of 1 indexed file(s) against 4 pattern(s); found nothing

findings.remediation_hint: Replace the digest with a purpose-built password hash (bcrypt, argon2, scrypt). Existing hashes cannot be converted, so rehash on next successful login and force a reset for accounts that never return.

findings.message: No SQL statement in source found, so this control has nothing to protect.

findings.remediation_hint: Pass values as query parameters, not as parts of the query string: cursor.execute("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = %s", (user_id,)) rather than an f-string. Table and column names cannot be parameterised, so map them through an allowlist instead of interpolating.

findings.control_name: Administrative routes carry a role check
findings.message: No administrative route found, so this control has nothing to protect.

evidence.note: searched 1 indexed file(s) for administrative route; 0 matched

findings.remediation_hint: Add an authorisation check distinct from the authentication one, and make it deny by default: derive the requirement from the resource rather than from the URL, so a new admin route is protected without anyone remembering to decorate it.

findings.control_name: Environment files excluded from version control
findings.message: No .env file present in the tree.

evidence.note: searched 4 file(s) for a .env; found none (.env.example and friends are ignored by design)

findings.remediation_hint: Add .env (and its per-environment variants) to .gitignore, commit a .env.example carrying names but no values, and rotate anything the real file already exposed.
